result.process_summary: Both the student and the machine‑learning model first acquire knowledge from a limited set of examples. In the source, the student memorizes each exact question‑answer pair, ignoring broader concepts. In the target, the model captures exact training‑set patterns, including noise. This leads to strong performance on the familiar data (the past quiz or training set) but a failure to apply knowledge to new, varied situations, reflecting poor generalization.
potential_breaks: Human memorization is a deliberate, conscious strategy, whereas overfitting is typically an unintended consequence of model capacity or training procedure.
The source mentions "typos and irrelevant details," which may not map cleanly onto statistical noise in data.
A student can later choose to study concepts, while a model requires explicit regularization; the analogy does not capture the role of corrective interventions.
